findings.title: Coverage compares different database snapshots
findings.description: The CLI supplies an autocommit connection, so ledger and raw-count queries see separate snapshots. If an ingest commits between these queries, coverage compares old ledger totals with new raw rows and incorrectly reports corruption, exiting 3. Read the manifest, ledger and raw counts within one read-only, repeatable-read transaction. Add a regression test that commits an ingest between reads.

findings.title: An unknown availability edge can report caught up
findings.description: With a configured tier/start, no explicit end and no observed edge, `wanted` becomes `None`. Nevertheless, this call passes `wanted=True`. On an empty manifest, `caught_up([])` returns `True`, despite the wanted horizon being unknown. Explicitly represent that uncertainty rather than declaring success, and test this configuration.

findings.title: Coverage repeatedly scans all instrument/session totals
findings.description: Each session scans and materializes both entire dictionaries, making report construction quadratic in session count. This runs synchronously inside `build_coverage`, blocking the event loop. An isolated check with 50,000 totals took approximately 1.8 ms for just one session, exceeding the required sub-millisecond synchronous-work bound. Group totals by session once, offload substantial processing, and add realistic load coverage.
